question: Can a single end-to-end Transformer map a document image directly to structured output without an OCR engine, and match OCR-based document understanding models in accuracy and speed?
hypothesis: A simple encoder-decoder pre-trained to read text (pseudo-OCR next-token prediction) avoids OCR cost, inflexibility and error propagation while matching or beating OCR-dependent VDU models.
contributions: A novel OCR-free VDU approach, first OCR-free Transformer trained end to end.
A simple pre-training scheme that uses synthetic data (SynthDoG), extendable to multiple languages.
Experiments on public benchmarks and private industrial datasets showing state-of-the-art results and cost advantages.
Code, pre-trained model and synthetic data released.

method.summary: Donut pairs a Swin-B visual encoder with the first four layers of a multilingual BART decoder. It is pre-trained to read all text in a page image (next-token cross-entropy) on IIT-CDIP with CLOVA-OCR pseudo labels plus SynthDoG synthetic pages, then fine-tuned so each downstream task (classification, information extraction, DocVQA) is a JSON token sequence generated from a task prompt.
method.task: visual document understanding: document classification, information extraction (parsing to JSON), document VQA

datasets.name: IIT-CDIP
datasets.source: Lewis et al. IIT-CDIP; pseudo text labels from commercial CLOVA OCR API
datasets.preprocessing: text labels from CLOVA OCR API

datasets.name: SynthDoG synthetic pages
datasets.size: 0.5M samples per language (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, English); 2M total
datasets.source: Generated from Wikipedia text, ImageNet backgrounds, collected paper textures, Noto fonts
datasets.preprocessing: random layout grids, blur, elastic distortion, perspective, shadow, JPEG compression

datasets.name: CORD
datasets.size: 0.8K train, 0.1K valid, 0.1K test receipt images; 30 unique fields

datasets.name: Ticket (Chinese train tickets)
datasets.split: 10% of train held out as validation

datasets.name: Business Card (in-service)
datasets.size: 20K train, 0.3K valid, 0.3K test Japanese business cards; 11 fields

datasets.name: Receipt (in-service)
datasets.size: 40K train, 1K valid, 1K test Korean receipts; 81 unique fields

datasets.name: DocVQA
datasets.split: 40K train, 5K valid, 5K test questions; test scored via evaluation site

models.name: Donut
models.init_from: decoder from multilingual BART (asian-bart-ecjk); encoder from ImageNet-pretrained Swin-B in the backbone study
models.tokenizer: BART subword tokens plus added special tokens per task ([START *], [END *], class tokens)
models.layers: Swin layer numbers {2, 2, 14, 2}; decoder 4 BART layers

other.input_resolution_960x1280: Train Tickets and Business Card fine-tuning
other.pretrain_note: ImageNet init of encoder is stated for the backbone comparison (Fig 7b), not explicitly for the main model

models.name: BERT / RoBERTa / LayoutLM / LayoutLMv2 / BROS / SPADE / WYVERN with OCR
models.architecture: OCR then Transformer encoder (BIO tagging or span prediction); WYVERN encoder-decoder; SPADE graph-based

other.ocr_engines: CLOVA OCR for most IE data, PaddleOCR for Ticket, MS OCR for LayoutLM-family timing on classification and VQA

training.objective: pre-training: cross-entropy of next-token prediction conditioned on image and previous text (read all text in reading order); fine-tuning: cross-entropy on JSON token sequence, teacher forcing
training.lr: pre-training initial 1e-4; fine-tuning selected from 1e-5 to 1e-4
training.lr_schedule: learning rate decreased as training progresses (form not given)
training.regularisation: gradient clipping, max norm selected from 0.05 to 1.0
training.hardware: 64 A100 GPUs for pre-training; baselines on P40, V100 or A100
training.compute: pre-training about 2-3 GPU days (as printed); 1280x960 fine-tune on CORD or Ticket about 0.5 hours on one A100; DocVQA about one GPU day and RVL-CDIP about two GPU days with 64 A100 at 2560x1920

other.fine_tune_selection: monitor edit distance over token sequences
other.fine_tune_init: all fine-tuning starts from the pre-trained multilingual model
other.DonutProto: smaller preliminary run: SynthDoG 1.2M, 8 V100 for 5 days, input 2048x1536; RVL-CDIP 94.5, CORD 85.4

inference.decoding: autoregressive generation from a task prompt token; malformed output treated as field lost (e.g. [START name] without [END name])
inference.prompting: special prompt tokens per task, e.g. <classification>, <parsing>, <vqa><question>...</question><answer>

other.speed_hardware: speed measured on a P40 GPU
other.output_conversion: regular expressions turn token sequence into JSON

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: classification accuracy on the RVL-CDIP test set

metrics.name: Field-level F1
metrics.definition: extracted field counts as correct only if exact match with ground truth; ignores partial overlap and structure

metrics.name: TED-based accuracy
metrics.definition: max(0, 1 - TED(pr, gt)/TED(empty, gt)) on trees

metrics.name: ANLS
metrics.definition: Average Normalized Levenshtein Similarity, edit-distance-based, DocVQA test via evaluation site

metrics.name: Time
metrics.definition: inference time per image, Donut on P40; OCR-based baselines include OCR

eval.protocol: Single reported number per cell; no seeds, variances or significance tests stated. LayoutLM-family VQA and classification scores copied from the LayoutLMv2 paper.

availability.weights: pre-trained model released at the same GitHub
availability.data: SynthDoG synthetic data released; CORD and Ticket public; Business Card and Receipt private

limits: Higher input resolution gives more robust accuracy but costs more; the authors use the original Transformer and note efficient attention may avoid this.
Donut misses tiny text in large images due to input resolution (Fig 6, right example).
On DocVQA Donut trails LayoutLMv2 (67.5 vs 78.1 ANLS) and the QG-trained large model (86.7).
Real IIT-CDIP images mattered for DocVQA, probably due to distribution similarity.
Single-run numbers with no seeds or variance reported; Business Card and Receipt data are private.
Speed comparisons mix Donut on a P40 with API OCR timings; OCR-based baselines' parameter counts exclude the OCR (+alpha).
Authors name enhancing the pre-training objective as future work.

terms.definition: modeling a direct mapping from a raw input image to the desired output without OCR

figures.caption: The pipeline overview and benchmarks. The proposed end-to-end model, Donut, outperforms the recent OCR-dependent VDU models in memory, time cost and accuracy.
figures.why: shows OCR pipeline versus single model and the speed/memory/accuracy gap at a glance

figures.caption: The pipeline of Donut. The encoder maps a given document image into embeddings. With the encoded embeddings, the decoder generates a sequence of tokens that can be converted into a target type of information in a structured form
figures.why: prompt tokens and JSON output per task

figures.caption: Analysis on (a) pre-training strategies, (b) image backbones, and (c) input resolutions. Performances on CORD and DocVQA are shown
Comparison of BERT, LayoutLMv2 and Donut on CORD. The performances (i.e., speed and accuracy) of the OCR-based models extremely varies depending on what OCR engine is used
figures.why: OCR engine sensitivity and low-data curve
